name: Heart and Cardiovascular Protection
blurb: Heart attack, stroke, heart failure and the outcome trials behind each drug.
title: Heart and Cardiovascular Protection
answer: Heart disease is the leading cause of death in people with diabetes, so drugs are now judged on whether they prevent heart attacks, strokes and heart failure, not just on glucose. Semaglutide, injectable and oral, has shown cardiovascular benefit, tirzepatide has shown cardiovascular safety against an active comparator, and SGLT2 inhibitors reduce heart failure.

explainer:
Cardiovascular outcome trials enrol thousands of people at high risk and follow them for years to count major adverse cardiovascular events, usually cardiovascular death, heart attack and stroke. Since 2008 regulators have required diabetes drugs to show they do not raise this risk, and several have gone further and shown they lower it.

Noninferiority and superiority are different results. A noninferior drug is shown not to be worse than its comparator by more than a set margin; a superior drug is shown to be better. When a new drug is compared with an active drug that already protects the heart, as tirzepatide was with dulaglutide, noninferiority is a meaningful result but not proof of extra benefit.

developments.text: SOUL showed oral semaglutide reduced major cardiovascular events by about 14 percent against placebo in high risk type 2 diabetes.
SURPASS-CVOT showed tirzepatide was noninferior to dulaglutide for major cardiovascular events.
